chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Habib narrated from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad ibn Mudarrib, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a pile of wheat that has been plastered (with clay/mud), do I pray upon it? He said, 'Do not pray upon it.' I said, 'For it is like a flat roof, level.' He said, 'Do not pray upon it.'
And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:

key_terms.السَّطْح: The flat roof of a house
key_terms.كُدْس: A pile or heap of grain
key_terms.مُطَيَّنٍ: Plastered or coated (typically with clay or mud)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying on a plastered pile of grain?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits praying on a plastered pile of wheat (*kuds*), even when level like a roof, primarily due to concerns regarding the stability of the surface and the potential for ritual impurity (*najasah*) from the plaster or underlying material. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *istiqrar* (stability) and *taharah* (purity) in the place of prostration, ensuring the worshipper is not distracted or defiled during prayer. The text notes that this specific prohibition does not contradict other narrations, indicating a nuanced application of rules based on the specific material properties of the surface.
